text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the oldest merged PR first. It’s the fastest way to validate the tool’s accuracy against real historical data without risking new reviews. The trade-off is delayed feedback on newer PRs, but we prioritize proving the tool works before scaling it up.

name: Gauge
text: Running PR-Agent in shadow mode on the oldest merged PR may not effectively validate its accuracy, as it may not account for new edge cases that have arisen since then. A better approach might be to run it on a mix of old and new PRs to get a more comprehensive understanding of its performance. This argument would be settled by reviewing the PR-Agent's performance metrics on a representative sample of PRs, which would provide concrete evidence of its accuracy and reliability.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest merged PR first to catch current edge cases early, then expand to older PRs only if the tool flags no critical issues. This cuts validation time by focusing on the most relevant data upfront while still covering historical context if needed.

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest *open* PR first. It catches routing flaws immediately—no waiting for merges—so we see how the tool handles live, unfiltered PRs right away. The trade-off is we risk no data if that PR closes before review, but we prioritize catching edge cases in current workflows over historical validation.

name: Ratchet
text: DECISION: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest open PR first, then expand to oldest merged PRs only if no critical issues surface. Result: validated tool performance on live data with minimal risk; owner Overhaul.
